title: Marvelous Designer for Linux is Here.
content:
![8eedb3d57bd545a7a4cf8d05e1a0a4bd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/0b6e9f44f1da4334bac30e59dbdf23d1/images/8eedb3d57bd545a7a4cf8d05e1a0a4bdSocial%20media%20image%20english.png)

We’re excited to announce that Marvelous Designer is now available on Linux. [_Download it here_](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/product/download) to get started, or sign up for a [_free trial._](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/product/trial/form)

This release supports Rocky Linux 9, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, and equivalent distributions, making it easier than ever for professional artists to integrate Marvelous Designer seamlessly into their Linux-based 3D pipelines.

* * *

  


YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ImTbgQFxEdQ?start=0

# **What’s New in the Linux Release?**

The Linux version has been designed with stability, simulation accuracy, and efficient workflows in mind. In addition to all the latest Marvelous Designer features, it also introduces a Python API, allowing users to:

  * Write and run scripts directly inside Marvelous Designer

  * Batch import and export files

  * Adjust simulation settings

  * Automate repetitive tasks

  * And more!




With these enhancements, Marvelous Designer is more powerful than ever for teams looking to streamline workflows and optimize production.

* * *

For technical specifications, licensing details, and more, visit our website or contact us at [_sales@marvelousdesigner.com_](https://mailto:sales@marvelousdesigner.com).

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Where? I go to click download and it says "Download Not Available".
Reply 1: The Linux version of Marvelous Designer is currently available only for Enterprise users. If you’re using a Personal license, the download option will not be accessible. Thank you for your understanding.

Comment 2: Look forward to it! 👍🏻
content_description: Discover the new Linux version of Marvelous Designer, designed for seamless integration into 3D workflows, offering enhanced features like a Python API for automation and improved simulation accuracy.

title: Marvelous Designer Standalone License Transition
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/49bf23b949ac4f80b4d2f8fa8f614643/images/43c34762130d455cbe34602a4e24e218Selected%20September%2030%202025%20.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/49bf23b949ac4f80b4d2f8fa8f614643/images/974e853e744f468398b0765f67757aabdefault_thumbnail.jpg)Hello Marvelous Designer Users,

We are transitioning to a consolidated, **account-based licensing model** without node-lock, ensuring a consistent and reliable experience for all users. This change also allows us to continue improving compatibility and rolling out ongoing enhancements, including support for the Linux operating system.

* * *

#### **Key Changes**

As of the effective date, the **Marvelous Designer Standalone Online license** will be retired and will no longer be available for purchase.

Please note that all existing Standalone licenses will continue to be fully supported and will retain all current features until their expiration date.

#### **Special Transition Offer**

To ensure a smooth transition, we have a special offer for our Annual Standalone license holders. You can renew your license to a **Network Online** license for the same price as your current Annual Standalone license during the grace period.

* * *

For more information, please refer to the [Marvelous Designer Standalone License Transition page](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/51136941117849-Marvelous-Designer-Standalone-License-Transition).

Thank you for your continued support.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to inform Marvelous Designer users about the transition to a consolidated account-based licensing model, highlighting key changes, ongoing support for existing licenses, and a special offer for license renewal.

title: UV Maps export and import in MD.
content:
I am experiencing issues with texture and opacity, as well as other map scaling, in Marvelous Designer.

My workflow:

In the UV Editor, I first arranged and fitted all patterns into the default 0–1 tile.

I then moved specific patterns into separate UV tiles and scaled them to maximum size.

I exported UV snapshots for all tiles at 2K resolution.

In external photo-editing software, I added details to each pattern and saved the images at the same resolution (2K, PNG/JPEG).

Back in Marvelous Designer, I assigned different fabrics to each pattern and applied the corresponding images as texture and opacity maps in the Property Editor.

The issue:

(The applied textures do not align consistently with the UVs. For each pattern, I need to manually scale the texture in the Property Editor through a trial-and-error method, and the required scaling is not uniform across all patterns.

Additional note:

If I select Texture Mapping "Unified," then I can't scale the Normal map

This issue did not occur in previous versions of Marvelous Designer (ver. 4 and prior), where the same workflow produced correct texture alignment without additional scaling.

Is there a recommended workflow to avoid this issue? Or can you provide guidance on the correct workflow?

Thanks

![d18379edecdd43218abc72552a8a9534](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/4a3b51da2334458f9a7c649bc34ced50/images/d18379edecdd43218abc72552a8a9534uv%20scaleing%20issue-1.jpg)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Use this website to report the issues and share the project with the map files. This way will be faster and easier for us to understand the issue. https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/4a3b51da2334458f9a7c649bc34ced50

Comment 2: At the property editor, you can see the Texture Mapping option, check the Unified option instead of Repeat.
Reply 1: Thanks, If I check Unified Option, Then I cant resize/scale Normal Maps, I am using default MD normal Maps for texture weave
Reply 2: Thank you! This small but important thing was a life saver for me!!! 🙏🏻
content_description: This webpage aims to provide guidance and solutions for resolving texture and opacity alignment issues in Marvelous Designer, particularly when working with UV mapping and scaling in version 5 and later.

title: Textures mapping For Front and Back side
content:
I want to apply two different texture maps to a single geometry surface: a lace texture (PNG with transparency) on the front face, and a different texture (PNG/jpeg) on the back face. This ensures that when viewing the object, the front renders the lace pattern with see-through effect, while the back renders independently with its own texture, eliminating the need for duplicated geometry or additional overlay patterns.

So that the front face provides the “see-through” lace effect, while the back face displays an independent texture map.

Note: I applied different texture maps to the fabric in the fabric property editor. 

Full transparency from the front view and not backside view

Your help will help others CLO Users also

![607bed3ff83f44a389885d46662be338](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/6936e1cc896f4cb99884a9c87f283a34/images/607bed3ff83f44a389885d46662be338clo%20community.JPG)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: When it comes to creating Lace with a background that's visible due to transparency, the key is knowing in which direction the normals of those faces are reflected.When you use the first technique described, creating a copy of the Front Pattern to place behind it, the normals are in the same direction, so you can see what's behind the first layer.Now, when you apply Thickness to the Fabric, you can apply individual materials for the Front, Back, and Sides. The normals in this case are facing outward, so even if you apply a different material, the transparency won't be reflected on the back side.Currently, for what you're looking for, you must work with sublayers to achieve the desired result.
content_description: This webpage aims to guide CLO users in applying distinct texture maps—one for a transparent lace effect on the front face and another for a separate texture on the back face of a single geometry surface, enhancing visual complexity without duplicating geometry.
